insight.title: The Safety Paradox
insight.subtitle: The hidden thermostat governing your risks.

sections.text: Do you drive faster when you feel safe? Our brains operate on a "risk thermostat." When safety increases, we subconsciously compensate by pushing harder, often neutralizing the very security we just acquired.

This is the Peltzman Effect. It is a biological feedback loop where your perception of safety dictates your behavior. The more "protected" you feel, the less cautious you naturally become within that system.
You see this everywhere: advanced software leads to more distractions; robust backup plans lead to sloppier execution. We rarely use safety to be safer; we usually use it to move faster.
Try this today: When you feel most confident about a choice, pause for five seconds. Ask yourself: "Am I actually being efficient, or am I just being less careful because I feel secure?"
True risk often hides exactly where you feel most protected.

news.title: Trump Expands Iran Threat as Deadline for Deal Nears
news.description: The U.S. has told Iran to open the crucial Strait of Hormuz to all shipping traffic or see power plants and bridges wiped out, sparking warnings about possible war crimes
news.why: Blocked shipping routes will likely drive up your monthly grocery bills.

news.title: Stocks stumble, oil above $110 as Trump's Iran deadline nears
news.description: Investors in wait-and-see mode ahead of Trump's deadline; Iran rejects ceasefire deal, seeks permanent end to war; Nikkei trades flat after early gains, South Korea up 0.2% after 2.5% surge; US futures fall 0.35%, Europe set for higher open
news.why: Surging oil prices mean filling your gas tank will cost more tomorrow.

news.title: Nigeria's Dangote refinery boosts exports to ease Africa's supply crunch
news.description: Nigeria's Dangote refinery, Africa's largest, has increased exports of gasoline and urea to African countries hit by supply disruptions caused by the Iran war, its owner Aliko ​Dangote said on Monday.
news.why: Increased refinery production could lower the price of fuel and groceries.

news.title: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff to engineers: Your role is not disappearing, it is just…
news.description: Tech News News: Salesforce's 15,000 engineers are not going anywhere—but what they do every day is changing fast. CEO Marc Benioff, speaking on The Future Live with M.
news.why: Tech workers must master AI tools to protect their current paychecks.

news.title: Teens turn to AI role-play chatbots, raising concerns over dependency and safety
news.description: Apps like Character.AI and Talkie reshape digital habits, raising questions around dependency, safety and social impact.
news.why: Your teenager may stop talking to friends to chat with AI bots.

news.title: Kano Targets 3.2 Million Children in Fresh Polio Vaccination Drive
news.description: The Kano State government has announced plans to vaccinate over 3,261,525 children aged zero to 59 months in a renewed effort to prevent polio-related diseases across the state.
news.why: Health workers visiting homes will prevent local children from facing lifelong paralysis.

news.title: Delhi doctor outlines five sleep patterns affecting long-term wellbeing
news.description: World Health Day 2026: An internal medicine expert explains five major sleep patterns and their impact on heart health, immunity, metabolism and mental wellbeing. Learn how short sleep, fragmented rest, delayed timing and oversleeping can raise health risks, and why maintaining a consistent sleep routine is essential for long-term balance and energy.
news.why: Improving your sleep habits now prevents expensive heart doctor visits later.

news.title: AIIMS and GMPSF Host 16th India Probiotic Symposium, Spotlighting Gut Health's Growing Role in Preventive Healthcare
news.description: New Delhi [India], April 7: The All-India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), in collaboration with the Gut Microbiota and Probiotic Science Foundation (India), hosted the 16th India Probiotic Symposium on March 27-28, 2026 at the Jawaharlal Nehru Auditorium, AIIMS, New Delhi. The symposium, themed 'Gut Microbiome and Probiotics: Impact from Cradle to Centenarians,' brought together leading clinicians, researchers and global experts, to deliberate on the expanding role of microbiome science, in preventive and clinical healthcare.
news.why: Eating specific probiotic foods can reduce your number of annual sick days.
